description: A non-selective beta-blocker with Class III antiarrhythmic potassium channel-blocking properties, used for ventricular arrhythmias and maintaining sinus rhythm in atrial fibrillation.
mechanism_of_action: D- and L-isomers block beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptors; D-isomer selectively blocks rapid delayed rectifier potassium current (IKr), prolonging myocardial action potential duration and effective refractory period.

description: A non-selective beta-adrenergic blocker with potent intrinsic sympathomimetic activity (ISA), lowering blood pressure with minimal resting bradycardia or metabolic suppression.
mechanism_of_action: Partial agonist at beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic receptors (intrinsic sympathomimetic activity - ISA); competitively blocks catecholamines during exercise/stress while providing low-level basal receptor stimulation at rest.

description: A phosphinic acid-containing ACE inhibitor prodrug characterized by dual, compensatory hepatic and renal elimination, eliminating the need for dose reductions in renal impairment.
mechanism_of_action: Hydrolyzed in the liver and gastrointestinal mucosa to fosinoprilat, which competitively inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), blocking conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II and preventing bradykinin degradation.

description: A lipophilic bicyclic prodrug ACE inhibitor with high vascular tissue ACE affinity and endothelial protective actions, used for hypertension and heart failure.
mechanism_of_action: De-esterified in the liver to active quinaprilat, a potent competitive inhibitor of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE); exhibits extremely high affinity and binding to tissue-bound ACE in vascular endothelium.

description: An ultra-lipophilic, long-acting non-sulfhydryl ACE inhibitor prodrug proven in the TRACE trial to significantly reduce mortality, sudden cardiac death, and progression to severe heart failure post-MI.
mechanism_of_action: Bioactivated in the liver by ester cleavage to trandolaprilat, an exceptionally potent, slow-dissociating competitive inhibitor of ACE with high tissue affinity; blocks angiotensin II formation and promotes bradykinin-mediated vasodilation.

description: A potent non-sulfhydryl ACE inhibitor prodrug proven to slow the progression of chronic renal insufficiency in non-diabetic kidney disease (AIPRI trial).
mechanism_of_action: Cleaved by hepatic esterases to active benazeprilat, which competitively inhibits ACE, preventing conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II and reducing sympathetic outflow and aldosterone production.

description: A potent, non-peptide AT1-receptor blocker with insurmountable binding and high oral bioavailability (60-80%), proven to halt the progression of diabetic nephropathy (IDNT and IRMA-2 trials).
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and insurmountably blocks angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptors in vascular smooth muscle and the adrenal gland, blocking angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone synthesis.

description: A non-biphenyl, non-tetrazole AT1-receptor blocker with dual postsynaptic AT1 and presynaptic sympathoinhibitory properties, effective for isolated systolic hypertension and stroke prevention (MOSES trial).
mechanism_of_action: Competitively and selectively blocks AT1 receptors postsynaptically, preventing angiotensin II vasoconstriction; uniquely blocks presynaptic AT1 receptors on sympathetic nerve terminals, inhibiting norepinephrine release and sympathetic tone.

description: An advanced ester prodrug ARB with the tightest, longest-lasting AT1-receptor binding kinetics in its class, delivering superior 24-hour blood pressure reduction compared to valsartan and olmesartan.
mechanism_of_action: Rapidly hydrolyzed by esterases in the gastrointestinal tract and liver to active azilsartan; binds with exceptional affinity and an extremely slow dissociation rate to the AT1 receptor, providing insurmountable and sustained receptor blockade.

description: A highly lipophilic, third-generation dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that integrates into the cell membrane lipid bilayer, providing smooth 24-hour vasodilation with minimal pedal oedema.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits transmembrane calcium influx through L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle; high lipophilicity causes it to dissolve in the membrane lipid bilayer, creating a local drug reservoir that diffuses slowly to receptor sites.

description: A second-generation dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with exceptional vascular selectivity (100:1 vascular to cardiac smooth muscle ratio), used once daily in extended-release form for hypertension and angina.
strengths: 2.5 mg ER; 5 mg ER; 10 mg ER
mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks voltage-gated L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle cells, inhibiting calcium influx and causing arteriolar dilation; has 100-fold higher selectivity for vascular smooth muscle than myocardial tissue.

description: A classical dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker proven in the landmark Syst-Eur trial to reduce stroke by 42% and vascular dementia by 50% in elderly patients with isolated systolic hypertension.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits L-type calcium channel current in vascular smooth muscle, decreasing intracellular calcium availability and producing arteriolar vasodilation and reduced total peripheral resistance.

description: A potent quinazoline-sulfonamide diuretic that acts on the proximal and distal tubules, uniquely retaining efficacy even in advanced renal failure (eGFR < 30 mL/min) and creating massive synergy with loop diuretics.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits sodium and chloride reabsorption in the cortical diluting segment of the distal convoluted tubule and proximal tubule; unique quinazoline structure allows it to remain active at low glomerular filtration rates.

description: A prototypical carbonic anhydrase inhibitor that blocks bicarbonate reabsorption in the proximal tubule, used for acute mountain sickness, glaucoma, metabolic alkalosis, and idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
strengths: 250 mg; 500 mg SR; 500 mg IV vial
dosage_forms: Tablet; Extended-Release Capsule; Powder for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Non-competitively and reversibly inhibits carbonic anhydrase (predominantly CA-II and CA-IV) in the renal proximal tubule, ciliary body of the eye, and choroid plexus; blocks H+ ion exchange for Na+, promoting urinary excretion of bicarbonate, sodium, potassium, and water.

description: An active organic nitrate vasodilator with 100% oral bioavailability and zero hepatic first-pass metabolism, providing predictable long-term prophylaxis for stable coronary artery disease.
mechanism_of_action: Denitrated intracellularly in vascular smooth muscle to release nitric oxide (NO); NO stimulates soluble guanylyl cyclase, increasing cyclic GMP (cGMP), leading to dephosphorylation of myosin light chains and marked venodilation.

description: An organic nitrate vasodilator used sublingually for acute angina relief and orally combined with hydralazine (BiDil) to significantly reduce mortality in Black patients with heart failure (A-HeFT trial).
strengths: 5 mg sublingual; 10 mg; 20 mg; 40 mg SR
dosage_forms: Sublingual Tablet; Immediate-Release Tablet; Sustained-Release Tablet
mechanism_of_action: Releases free nitric oxide in vascular smooth muscle, stimulating guanylyl cyclase to produce cGMP; selectively dilates venous capacitance vessels to decrease preload, and dilates large epicardial coronary arteries.

description: The foundational rapid-acting organic nitrate vasodilator used sublingually for immediate termination of acute angina attacks and intravenously for acute heart failure, pulmonary oedema, and hypertensive emergencies.
strengths: 0.4 mg (400 mcg) sublingual tablet; 0.4 mg/metered dose sublingual spray; 5 mg/mL (5 mL, 10 mL IV ampoules); 2.5 mg, 6.5 mg sustained release; 5 mg/24h, 10 mg/24h transdermal patch; 2% ointment
dosage_forms: Sublingual Tablet; Sublingual Aerosol Spray; Solution for Injection / Infusion; Transdermal Patch; Topical Ointment
mechanism_of_action: Denitrated in vascular smooth muscle by mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH-2) to release nitric oxide (NO); stimulates guanylyl cyclase, increasing intracellular cGMP and causing profound venous dilation, lowering preload and ventricular wall stress; dilates coronary collaterals.

description: A dual-action potassium channel opener and organic nitrate donor that provides balanced arterial and venous dilation without developing nitrate tolerance, proven to reduce major coronary events (IONA study).
mechanism_of_action: Dual mechanism: opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels (K-ATP) in arterial smooth muscle causing hyperpolarization and arteriolar dilation (reduces afterload and mimics ischemic preconditioning), AND contains a nitrate moiety that donates nitric oxide (NO) causing venodilation (reduces preload) and coronary vasodilation.

description: A first-in-class late inward sodium current (INa-late) inhibitor that reduces intracellular calcium overload in ischemic cardiomyocytes, improving myocardial perfusion without lowering heart rate or blood pressure.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits the late inward sodium current (late INa) in ischemic myocardial cells, preventing sodium accumulation, reversing reverse Na+/Ca2+ exchange, and attenuating intracellular calcium overload; reduces diastolic wall tension and mechanical compression of microvascular coronary vessels.

description: A cellular anti-ischemic metabolic agent that shifts myocardial energy metabolism from fatty acid oxidation to glucose oxidation, protecting cardiomyocytes against ischemia without hemodynamic effects.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits mitochondrial long-chain 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (3-KAT), suppressing fatty acid beta-oxidation; shifts cellular energy production toward glucose oxidation, which requires less oxygen per ATP molecule produced, optimizing cardiomyocyte energy during ischemia.

description: A potent direct-acting antiviral targeting HCV non-structural protein 5A (NS5A), combined with sofosbuvir for pan-genotypic Hepatitis C cures.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to the N-terminus of Domain I of the HCV NS5A replication complex, inhibiting both viral RNA replication and virion assembly.

description: A targeted nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) prodrug delivering higher intracellular levels with 90% lower systemic tenofovir exposure, reducing renal and bone toxicities.
mechanism_of_action: Hydrolyzed intracellularly by carboxylesterase 1 (CES1) and cathepsin A in PBMCs and hepatocytes to tenofovir, which is diphosphorylated to tenofovir diphosphate; inhibits HBV reverse transcriptase and HIV-1 reverse transcriptase by chain termination.

description: An oral acyclic nucleotide analogue used for chronic Hepatitis B, particularly effective against lamivudine-resistant YMDD mutant HBV strains.
mechanism_of_action: Diester prodrug converted intracellularly by esterases to adefovir, which is phosphorylated to adefovir diphosphate; competitively inhibits HBV DNA polymerase and causes chain termination.

description: A classical cytidine nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) used in combination regimens for HIV-1 infection and as a lower-dose agent for chronic Hepatitis B.
strengths: 100 mg (HBV); 150 mg; 300 mg (HIV); 10 mg/mL oral solution
mechanism_of_action: Phosphorylated intracellularly to lamivudine 5'-triphosphate, which competitively inhibits HIV-1 reverse transcriptase and HBV DNA polymerase, causing viral DNA chain termination.

description: The global broad-spectrum anthelmintic of choice for schistosomiasis, liver and lung flukes, and cestode (tapeworm) infections including neurocysticercosis.
mechanism_of_action: Increases cell membrane permeability to calcium ions in platyhelminths, producing rapid calcium influx, massive muscular contraction, paralysis, and tegumental vacuolization; dislodges parasites, exposing them to host immune attack.

description: A 5-nitroimidazole derivative with a longer half-life (14 hours) and lower neurotoxicity than metronidazole, widely used in India for amoebiasis, giardiasis, and anaerobic infections.
mechanism_of_action: Enters microbial cells by passive diffusion; nitro group is reduced by ferredoxin oxidoreductase into toxic free radicals that bind to bacterial and protozoan DNA, causing strand breakage and cell death.

description: A depolarizing neuromuscular blocking anthelmintic that paralyzes pinworms, roundworms, and hookworms in the intestinal lumen, expelled safely by normal peristalsis.
mechanism_of_action: Acts as a depolarizing neuromuscular junction blocker and nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist in nematodes; causes persistent muscular depolarization, spastic paralysis, and detachment from the intestinal wall.

description: A broad-spectrum hydroxypyridone antifungal with a unique metal ion-chelating mechanism, anti-inflammatory and antibacterial activity, used for onychomycosis, seborrheic dermatitis, and tinea.
dosage_forms: Nail Lacquer; Topical Cream; Medicated Shampoo; Topical Gel
mechanism_of_action: Chelates polyvalent cations (Fe3+ and Al3+), inhibiting metal-dependent enzymes (cytochromes, catalase, peroxidase) in fungal mitochondria; disrupts membrane transport and electron transport chains.

description: A classical polyene macrolide antifungal not absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract, serving as the gold standard topical and oral suspension treatment for oral candidiasis (thrush).
strengths: 100,000 units/mL oral suspension; 100,000 units/g topical cream; 100,000 units vaginal tablet
dosage_forms: Oral Suspension; Topical Cream; Topical Ointment; Vaginal Tablet
routes: Oral (Topical Swish and Swallow); Topical; Vaginal
mechanism_of_action: Binds irreversibly to ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming transmembrane pores and barrel-like channels that leak potassium and essential cellular constituents, causing fungal cell death.

description: An oral pyrazinecarboxamide antiviral prodrug that selectively inhibits viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), approved for novel or re-emerging pandemic influenza strains.
mechanism_of_action: Phosphoribosylated intracellularly to active favipiravir ribofuranosyltriphosphate (favipiravir-RTP), which selectively inhibits viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) or incorporates into viral RNA, causing chain termination and lethal mutagenesis.

description: A broad-spectrum Class III antiarrhythmic with electrophysiologic properties spanning all four Vaughan Williams classes, widely used for refractory ventricular and supraventricular arrhythmias.
strengths: 100 mg; 200 mg; 150 mg/3 mL IV ampoule
mechanism_of_action: Predominantly blocks myocardial outward potassium currents (IKr, IKs), prolonging action potential duration and refractory period; additionally blocks inactivated sodium channels (Class I), non-competitively blocks beta receptors (Class II), and inhibits L-type calcium channels (Class IV).

description: A potent Class IC antiarrhythmic with marked sodium channel blockade and slow dissociation kinetics, used as the first-line 'pill-in-the-pocket' for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation in structurally normal hearts.
mechanism_of_action: Markedly blocks open fast inward voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav1.5) with slow dissociation kinetics; significantly slows phase 0 depolarization and His-Purkinje conduction velocity; also blocks cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2), suppressing spontaneous calcium release from sarcoplasmic reticulum.

description: A Class IC antiarrhythmic with intrinsic mild beta-blocking and local anesthetic properties, used for maintaining sinus rhythm in atrial fibrillation and supraventricular tachycardias.
strengths: 150 mg; 300 mg; 225 mg SR; 325 mg SR; 425 mg SR
mechanism_of_action: Blocks fast inward sodium channels (Class IC) with slow recovery kinetics, slowing phase 0 depolarization; structurally similar to propranolol, exerting mild non-selective beta-adrenergic blockade (approx. 1/40th the potency of propranolol).

description: A non-iodinated benzofuran derivative of amiodarone designed to reduce multiorgan thyroid and pulmonary toxicities, used to maintain sinus rhythm in paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation.
mechanism_of_action: Exhibits multichannel antiarrhythmic activity across all four Vaughan Williams classes (blocks IKr, IKs, INa, ICa, and possesses non-competitive antiadrenergic activity); lacks the iodine moieties of amiodarone and incorporates a methane-sulfonyl group to reduce lipophilicity.

description: An endogenous purine nucleoside with an ultra-short half-life (<10 seconds) that transiently blocks AV nodal conduction, serving as the gold standard acute rescue agent for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT).
strengths: 3 mg/mL (2 mL vial = 6 mg, 4 mL vial = 12 mg)
dosage_forms: Solution for Rapid IV Bolus Injection
mechanism_of_action: Binds to myocardial purinergic A1 receptors coupled to Gi proteins, activating inward rectifier potassium channels (IK-Ado) and inhibiting adenylate cyclase-mediated L-type calcium influx; profoundly slows AV nodal conduction velocity and prolongs AV refractory periods.

description: An orally active Class IB antiarrhythmic and structural analogue of lidocaine, used for life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias, myotonic disorders (non-dystrophic myotonia), and neuropathic pain.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits fast inward voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav1.5 in myocardium, Nav1.4 in skeletal muscle), shortening action potential duration and effective refractory period in Purkinje fibers; accelerates repolarization and blocks persistent/late sodium currents (INa-late).

description: The quintessential Class IB antiarrhythmic and amide local anesthetic, administered intravenously for acute ventricular arrhythmias during myocardial infarction or cardiac arrest, and topically for regional anesthesia.
strengths: 2% IV vial (20 mg/mL); 1% IV vial (10 mg/mL); 2% topical gel; 5% transdermal patch; 10% aerosol spray
dosage_forms: Solution for Injection; Topical Gel; Transdermal Patch; Aerosol Spray
mechanism_of_action: Binds to the intracellular pore of voltage-gated fast sodium channels (Nav1.5) in cardiac tissue, preferentially binding to open and inactivated channels in depolarized, ischemic, or rapidly firing myocardium; shortens action potential duration and effective refractory period.

description: An oral direct factor Xa inhibitor (DOAC) taken once daily with the evening meal for stroke prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation and treatment/prevention of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively, reversibly, and competitively inhibits free and clot-bound factor Xa and prothrombinase activity; blocks the intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation pathways, preventing thrombin generation and fibrin clot propagation.

description: An oral direct factor Xa inhibitor (DOAC) taken twice daily, proven in the landmark ARISTOTLE trial to be superior to warfarin in reducing stroke, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality in atrial fibrillation.
mechanism_of_action: Potent, reversible, direct, and highly selective inhibitor of free and clot-bound factor Xa and prothrombinase; decreases thrombin generation and prevents fibrin thrombus development.

description: An oral direct thrombin (Factor IIa) inhibitor prodrug proven in the RE-LY trial to reduce stroke in non-valvular atrial fibrillation, featuring the rapid specific reversal antidote idarucizumab (Praxbind).
mechanism_of_action: Converted by systemic and hepatic esterases to active dabigatran, a potent, competitive, reversible, direct inhibitor of free and clot-bound thrombin (factor IIa); blocks thrombin-mediated cleavage of fibrinogen to fibrin monomers and inhibits thrombin-induced platelet aggregation.

description: A once-daily oral direct factor Xa inhibitor proven in the ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 trial for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and treatment of venous thromboembolism.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and competitively inhibits factor Xa, blocking the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin; inhibits both free and clot-associated factor Xa activity, suppressing coagulation cascades.

description: A synthetic pentasaccharide that selectively binds antithrombin III to inhibit factor Xa, providing parenteral anticoagulation without causing heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT).
strengths: 2.5 mg/0.5 mL; 5 mg/0.4 mL; 7.5 mg/0.6 mL; 10 mg/0.8 mL prefilled syringes
mechanism_of_action: Synthetic pentasaccharide sequence that selectively and irreversibly binds to antithrombin III (ATIII), inducing a conformational change that accelerates ATIII-mediated neutralization of factor Xa by 300-fold; does NOT inactivate thrombin (factor IIa) and does NOT bind to platelet factor 4 (PF4).

description: A classical parenteral glycosaminoglycan anticoagulant that binds antithrombin III to inactivate thrombin and factor Xa, serving as the gold standard titratable agent for cardiopulmonary bypass, hemodialysis, and acute thromboembolism.
mechanism_of_action: Binds via a unique pentasaccharide sequence to antithrombin III (ATIII), accelerating ATIII-mediated inactivation of thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa by 1,000-fold; requires a long polysaccharide chain (at least 18 saccharide units) to form a ternary bridge complex with thrombin.

description: A synthetic 20-amino acid parenteral direct thrombin inhibitor (hirudin analogue) with a 25-minute half-life, used as an alternative to heparin in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and HIT.
dosage_forms: Lyophilized Powder for Solution for Injection / Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Binds specifically, reversibly, and directly to both the catalytic site and the anion-binding exosite I of circulating and clot-bound thrombin (factor IIa); cleavage of the bivalirudin Arg3-Pro4 bond by thrombin slowly restores thrombin active site function.

description: A direct-acting, reversibly binding P2Y12 platelet inhibitor proven in the landmark PLATO trial to significantly reduce cardiovascular mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke compared to clopidogrel.
mechanism_of_action: Reversibly, allosterically, and non-competitively binds to the platelet P2Y12 adenosine diphosphate (ADP) receptor, locking the receptor in an inactive state; additionally inhibits equilibrative nucleoside transporter-1 (ENT1), increasing extracellular adenosine levels.

description: A potent, third-generation thienopyridine oral prodrug that irreversibly inhibits platelet P2Y12 receptors, proven in the TRITON-TIMI 38 trial to superiorly prevent stent thrombosis in acute coronary syndromes undergoing PCI.
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug rapidly hydrolyzed by intestinal carboxylesterases to a thiolactone intermediate (R-95913), then converted in a single hepatic step by CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 to active metabolite R-138727; irreversibly binds to platelet P2Y12 ADP receptors, permanently blocking ADP-mediated GPIIb/IIIa receptor activation.

description: A selective phosphodiesterase-3 (PDE3) inhibitor that suppresses platelet aggregation and produces arterial vasodilation, serving as the gold standard medical treatment for intermittent claudication.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase type 3 (PDE3), preventing cyclic AMP (cAMP) degradation in platelets and vascular smooth muscle; elevated cAMP activates protein kinase A (PKA), inhibiting platelet aggregation and producing potent arterial vasodilation; also inhibits vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation.

description: A phosphodiesterase inhibitor and adenosine reuptake blocker, combined with low-dose aspirin (Aggrenox) for secondary prevention of stroke, and used intravenously as a pharmacologic stress agent.
strengths: 25 mg; 50 mg; 75 mg; 200 mg ER (combined with 25 mg aspirin); 10 mg/2 mL IV ampoule
dosage_forms: Tablet; Extended-Release Capsule; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits the uptake of adenosine into erythrocytes, platelets, and endothelial cells, increasing extracellular adenosine concentrations; also inhibits cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterases (PDE5 and PDE3), increasing intracellular cAMP and cGMP; blocks thromboxane A2 synthesis.

description: A synthetic lysine analogue antifibrinolytic that reversibly blocks plasminogen activation, widely used to prevent and treat massive hemorrhage in trauma, surgery, and heavy menstrual bleeding.
strengths: 500 mg; 650 mg; 500 mg/5 mL IV ampoule; 1000 mg/10 mL IV ampoule
mechanism_of_action: Competitively and reversibly blocks the lysine-binding sites on plasminogen molecules, preventing plasminogen from binding to fibrin; inhibits the conversion of plasminogen to active plasmin and suppresses fibrin clot dissolution (fibrinolysis); at high concentrations, non-competitively inhibits plasmin.

description: A synthetic lysine analogue antifibrinolytic that competitively inhibits plasminogen activation, used for hyperfibrinolytic bleeding, cardiac surgery, and dental procedures in hemophiliacs.
strengths: 500 mg; 1000 mg; 250 mg/mL oral solution; 250 mg/mL (20 mL IV vial = 5 g)
dosage_forms: Tablet; Oral Solution; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Competitively inhibits plasminogen activators (tissue plasminogen activator and urokinase) and blocks the lysine-binding sites on plasminogen, preventing its conversion to active plasmin; at high concentrations, directly inhibits plasmin.

description: A substituted benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that suppresses gastric acid secretion, used for GERD, peptic ulcers, and H. pylori eradication.
strengths: 15 mg; 30 mg; 30 mg orally disintegrating tablet (ODT)
mechanism_of_action: Accumulates in the acidic secretory canaliculi of parietal cells and converts to active sulfenamide; irreversibly binds via disulfide bonds to the H+/K+-ATPase proton pump, blocking the final step of acid secretion.

description: An R-enantiomer proton pump inhibitor featuring Dual Delayed Release (DDR) technology, providing two distinct drug releases over 24 hours and flexible dosing without regard to meals.
mechanism_of_action: Pure (R)-enantiomer of lansoprazole; selectively inhibits gastric H+/K+-ATPase in parietal cells; unique Dual Delayed Release formulation contains two types of enteric-coated granules: the first release occurs in the duodenum at pH 5.5 (1-2 hours post-dose), and the second release occurs in the distal ileum at pH 6.75 (4-5 hours post-dose).

description: A novel third-generation proton pump inhibitor with an extended plasma half-life and non-enzymatic clearance, providing superior nocturnal acid suppression and minimal CYP2C19 drug interactions.
mechanism_of_action: Irreversibly inhibits the gastric parietal H+/K+-ATPase pump; contains a pyrrole ring substituent that prolongs binding to sulfhydryl groups on the enzyme, conferring slow dissociation and prolonged antisecretory action.

description: A potent, competitive histamine H2-receptor antagonist with high oral bioavailability (95-100%) and zero antiandrogenic or CYP450 inhibitory actions, used for peptic ulcers and reflux esophagitis.
mechanism_of_action: De-acetylated in the liver and small intestine to active roxatidine, which competitively and selectively blocks histamine H2 receptors on the basolateral membrane of gastric parietal cells; prevents histamine-induced adenylate cyclase activation and cAMP-mediated gastric acid secretion.

description: The historical prototype histamine H2-receptor antagonist, characterized by potent CYP450 enzyme inhibition and antiandrogenic properties, now largely superseded by cleaner H2 blockers.
mechanism_of_action: Competitively blocks histamine H2 receptors on parietal cells, reducing basal, nocturnal, and meal-stimulated gastric acid production; also binds to imidazole receptors and inhibits cytochrome P450 monooxygenases.

description: The levorotatory enantiomer of sulpiride with dual enteric dopamine D2-receptor antagonism and 5-HT4 receptor agonism, widely used in India for functional dyspepsia and diabetic gastroparesis.
strengths: 25 mg; 75 mg SR; 25 mg/2 mL injection
dosage_forms: Tablet; Sustained-Release Capsule; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks enteric and central dopamine D2 receptors, removing the inhibitory effect of dopamine on gastrointestinal motility; concurrently acts as an agonist at 5-HT4 receptors on enteric cholinergic motor neurons, stimulating acetylcholine release from the myenteric plexus.

description: A benzamide prokinetic with dual 5-HT4 agonism and 5-HT2 / D2 antagonism, used for functional dyspepsia and GERD with lower extrapyramidal risk than metoclopramide.
mechanism_of_action: Stimulates gastrointestinal 5-HT4 receptors, promotes acetylcholine release from myenteric plexus neurons, and blocks inhibitory 5-HT2 and dopamine D2 receptors; enhances gastrointestinal motor coordination.

description: A selective gastroprokinetic 5-HT4 receptor agonist completely devoid of dopamine D2 and 5-HT1/5-HT2 affinity, providing pure prokinetic relief without extrapyramidal or cardiac QT toxicities.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and potently stimulates 5-HT4 receptors on enteric cholinergic interneurons and motor neurons, stimulating intrinsic acetylcholine release from the myenteric plexus; lacks dopamine D2-receptor antagonist properties and does NOT block HERG potassium channels.

description: A potent, highly selective second-generation 5-HT3 receptor antagonist with a 9-hour half-life, used to prevent nausea and vomiting from emetogenic chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
strengths: 1 mg; 2 mg; 1 mg/mL IV ampoule; 3.1 mg/24h transdermal patch
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Solution for Injection; Transdermal Patch
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and competitively blocks serotonin 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents in the gastrointestinal tract and centrally in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) and solitary tract nucleus (NTS); blocks peripheral and central serotonin emetic signaling.

description: A potent second-generation 5-HT3 receptor antagonist with a 40-hour half-life and unique receptor allosteric binding, uniquely effective for both acute AND delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.
strengths: 0.5 mg capsule; 0.25 mg/5 mL IV vial
dosage_forms: Soft Gelatin Capsule; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: High-affinity competitive and allosteric 5-HT3 receptor antagonist (binds with 100-fold higher affinity than ondansetron and granisetron); induces 5-HT3 receptor internalization and cross-talk inhibition with substance P (NK1) pathways.

description: A long-acting neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist with an ultra-long 169-hour (7-day) half-life that does not inhibit CYP3A4, combined with a 5-HT3 antagonist and dexamethasone for highly emetogenic chemotherapy.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and competitively blocks substance P from binding to neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptors in the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) and solitary tract nucleus in the brainstem; does NOT inhibit or induce CYP3A4.

description: An unabsorbable, non-fermentable osmotic laxative that retains water in the intestinal lumen, serving as the gold standard first-line treatment for chronic constipation and bowel preparation.
strengths: 17 g powder sachet; 119 g, 255 g, 510 g bulk powder bottles
mechanism_of_action: High molecular weight linear polymer of ethylene glycol that forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules; remains entirely within the intestinal lumen without being absorbed, metabolized, or fermented by gut microbiota; creates an osmotic gradient that retains water inside the stool.

description: A locally acting stimulant laxative prodrug converted by colonic bacteria to active bis-(p-hydroxyphenyl)-pyridyl-2-methane (BHPM), used for constipation and bowel cleansing.
dosage_forms: Tablet; Oral Drops; Powder for Oral Solution (with Magnesium Citrate)
mechanism_of_action: Inert prodrug that traverses the stomach and small intestine unabsorbed; converted specifically in the colon by bacterial arylsulfatases into active bis-(p-hydroxyphenyl)-pyridyl-2-methane (BHPM); stimulates mucosal nerve endings (myenteric plexus), accelerating colonic peristalsis and reducing water absorption.

description: A first-in-class, highly selective 5-HT4 receptor agonist that stimulates high-amplitude propagating contractions (HAPCs), serving as the premier enterokinetic agent for chronic idiopathic constipation.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and potently binds to 5-HT4 receptors on enteric neurons (with >150-fold selectivity over all other 5-HT and dopamine receptors); triggers proximal colonic high-amplitude propagating contractions (HAPCs) and enhances colonic mass movements.

description: A 14-amino acid synthetic peptide guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) agonist that increases intestinal fluid secretion and decreases visceral pain, used for IBS with constipation (IBS-C).
mechanism_of_action: Binds to and activates guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C) receptors on the luminal surface of intestinal enterocytes, elevating intracellular cyclic GMP (cGMP); cGMP activates CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator), stimulating secretion of chloride and bicarbonate into the lumen, pulling water into the bowel; extracellular cGMP inhibits pain-sensing visceral nociceptive nerves.

description: A bicyclic fatty acid prostaglandin E1 derivative that selectively activates type-2 chloride channels (ClC-2), stimulating mucosal fluid secretion for chronic constipation, IBS-C, and opioid constipation.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively activates type-2 chloride channels (ClC-2) on the apical membrane of human intestinal epithelial cells, triggering active chloride and passive sodium/water efflux into the intestinal lumen; promotes mucosal healing and restores tight junction barrier integrity.

description: An oral enkephalinase inhibitor prodrug that prevents the breakdown of endogenous enkephalins, acting as a pure antisecretory antidiarrheal without slowing intestinal transit or causing rebound constipation.
strengths: 10 mg sachet; 30 mg sachet; 100 mg capsule
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug rapidly hydrolyzed by systemic esterases to thiorphan, an active inhibitor of neutral endopeptidase (enkephalinase); prevents the degradation of endogenous opioid enkephalins in the intestinal mucosal wall; elevated enkephalins activate delta-opioid receptors, selectively suppressing cholera toxin- and rotavirus-induced hypersecretion of water and electrolytes.

description: A dual-action anticholinergic and direct smooth muscle relaxant antispasmodic, used for intestinal colic, biliary colic, and abdominal cramping in irritable bowel syndrome.
strengths: 10 mg; 20 mg; 10 mg/5 mL syrup; 10 mg/mL injection
dosage_forms: Tablet; Capsule; Oral Syrup; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Acts via a dual mechanism: competitively antagonizes muscarinic M1, M2, and M3 acetylcholine receptors on visceral smooth muscle, AND exerts a direct, non-competitive musculotropic spasmolytic effect on smooth muscle fibers.

description: A selective phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor antispasmodic that relaxes visceral smooth muscle without anticholinergic side effects, widely used for biliary, renal, and gastrointestinal colic.
strengths: 40 mg; 80 mg; 40 mg/2 mL IV/IM ampoule
mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase type 4 (PDE4) in visceral smooth muscle cells, preventing cyclic AMP (cAMP) breakdown; elevated intracellular cAMP phosphorylates myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK), inactivating it and causing smooth muscle relaxation; completely lacks antimuscarinic activity.

description: A musculotropic antispasmodic with dual sodium-channel blocking and intracellular calcium store-depleting actions, specifically normalizing colonic motility in irritable bowel syndrome without systemic anticholinergic effects.
mechanism_of_action: Exerts a direct musculotropic antispasmodic action on gastrointestinal smooth muscle cells: blocks voltage-operated fast sodium channels (inhibiting spasm) AND inhibits calcium influx and intracellular calcium release from sarcoplasmic reticulum; also blocks noradrenaline reuptake locally.

description: A quaternary ammonium antispasmodic with dual L-type calcium channel and tachykinin NK2 receptor antagonism, acting locally in the gut lumen with near-zero systemic absorption for IBS.
mechanism_of_action: Triple action: blocks L-type and T-type voltage-gated calcium channels in intestinal smooth muscle cells, antagonizes tachykinin neurokinin-2 (NK2) receptors, and mildly antagonizes muscarinic M3 receptors in the colon wall.

description: A synergistic fixed-dose combination of a central anxiolytic benzodiazepine and a peripheral anticholinergic antispasmodic, used for stress-triggered irritable bowel syndrome and peptic ulcer disease.
mechanism_of_action: Chlordiazepoxide enhances GABA-A receptor opening frequency in the limbic system, dampening brain-gut stress axis activation and central anxiety; clidinium bromide competitively blocks muscarinic M3 receptors on gastrointestinal smooth muscle and secretory glands, suppressing bowel spasms and gastric acid.

description: A naturally occurring hydrophilic tertiary bile acid that displaces toxic hydrophobic bile salts, serving as the gold standard first-line disease-modifying treatment for primary biliary cholangitis (PBC).
mechanism_of_action: Multiple hepatoprotective mechanisms: replaces toxic hydrophobic bile acids (cholic, deoxycholic, chenodeoxycholic acid) in the circulating bile acid pool; stimulates hepatobiliary secretion and bicarbonate secretion ('bicarbonate umbrella'); suppresses hepatocyte and cholangiocyte apoptosis; solubilizes cholesterol into liquid-crystalline mesophases, promoting dissolution of cholesterol gallstones.

description: A potent semi-synthetic farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist that suppresses bile acid synthesis and enhances biliary output, used for primary biliary cholangitis unresponsive to UDCA.
mechanism_of_action: Binds directly and potently to the nuclear farnesoid X receptor (FXR) with 100-fold higher affinity than chenodeoxycholic acid; activation of FXR down-regulates cholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase (CYP7A1), the rate-limiting enzyme in bile acid synthesis, and up-regulates bile salt export pump (BSEP) and fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19).

description: A standardized botanical extract of Silybum marianum containing flavonolignans (silybin) with potent antioxidant, membrane-stabilizing, and antifibrotic hepatoprotective properties.
mechanism_of_action: Multiple hepatoprotective actions: scavenges free radicals, prevents lipid peroxidation of hepatocyte membranes, stimulates RNA polymerase I to accelerate ribosomal protein synthesis and liver regeneration, and inhibits nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-kB) to suppress inflammatory cytokines and hepatic stellate cell activation.

description: An ultra-long-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonist (ultra-LABA) providing fast-onset (5 minutes) and 24-hour bronchodilation for once-daily maintenance therapy in COPD.
mechanism_of_action: Selective agonist at beta-2 adrenergic receptors on bronchial smooth muscle; stimulates intracellular adenylate cyclase to convert ATP to cAMP, activating protein kinase A (PKA); reduces intracellular calcium and induces profound bronchial relaxation.

description: An ultra-long-acting beta-2 agonist (ultra-LABA) with 24-hour bronchodilation, co-formulated with fluticasone furoate (Breo) or umeclidinium (Anoro) in the once-daily Ellipta dry powder inhaler.
strengths: 25 mcg (co-formulated with fluticasone furoate or umeclidinium)
mechanism_of_action: Highly selective, long-acting beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; stimulates intracellular adenylate cyclase, elevating cyclic AMP; relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and inhibits release of inflammatory mediators from mast cells.

description: A once-daily ultra-long-acting beta-2 agonist delivered via the propellant-free Respimat Soft Mist Inhaler, providing 24-hour bronchodilation for COPD.
mechanism_of_action: Highly selective and potent beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; binds with high affinity to human beta-2 receptors (241-fold higher selectivity over beta-1); stimulates adenylate cyclase, elevating cAMP and relaxing airway smooth muscle.

description: A quaternary ammonium long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) with fast onset and high M3-receptor selectivity, used as once-daily maintenance for COPD and parenterally to reduce secretions.
strengths: 50 mcg inhalation capsule (Seebri Breezhaler); 0.2 mg/mL IV/IM vial; 1 mg, 2 mg oral tablets
dosage_forms: Inhalation Powder; Solution for Injection; Oral Tablet
mechanism_of_action: Quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic agent; competitively and reversibly blocks muscarinic M3 receptors on airway smooth muscle cells, inhibiting acetylcholine-induced bronchoconstriction; dissociates significantly faster from M2 receptors than M3 receptors, ensuring prolonged bronchodilation without tachycardia.

description: A long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) rapidly hydrolyzed in human plasma by butyrylcholinesterase, providing potent local bronchodilation with near-zero systemic anticholinergic side effects.
mechanism_of_action: Competitively and reversibly inhibits muscarinic M3 receptors in airway smooth muscle, blocking acetylcholine-mediated bronchoconstriction; possesses prolonged residence time at M3 receptors, but is rapidly broken down by esterases once it enters systemic circulation.

description: A once-daily long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) delivered via the intuitive Ellipta dry powder inhaler, providing 24-hour bronchodilation for COPD maintenance.
mechanism_of_action: Long-acting muscarinic receptor antagonist (anticholinergic); competitively blocks acetylcholine from binding to muscarinic M3 receptors in bronchial smooth muscle cells, preventing calcium-dependent airway constriction.

description: A synthetic halogenated glucocorticoid prodrug rapidly bioactivated in the lungs to active 17-BMP, delivered in extrafine solution aerosols for persistent asthma and allergic rhinitis.
strengths: 50 mcg; 100 mcg; 200 mcg per actuation (MDI); 50 mcg/actuation nasal spray
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug rapidly hydrolyzed in lung tissue by carboxylesterases to beclomethasone-17-monopropionate (17-BMP), which binds with 30-fold higher affinity to glucocorticoid receptors; translocates to the nucleus, inhibiting NF-kB and AP-1 transcription factors; down-regulates pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and adhesion molecules while up-regulating anti-inflammatory lipocortin-1 (annexin A1).

description: An on-site lung-activated steroid prodrug bioactivated in the bronchial epithelium with near-zero oral bioavailability (<1%), providing maximal asthma control with the lowest rates of oral thrush and hoarseness.
strengths: 80 mcg; 160 mcg per actuation (Alvesco pMDI); 50 mcg/actuation nasal spray (Omnaris)
mechanism_of_action: Inhaled as an inactive prodrug that is selectively cleaved by intracellular esterases in human lung tissue to active desisobutyryl-ciclesonide (des-CIC); des-CIC binds with 100-fold higher affinity to glucocorticoid receptors, suppressing pro-inflammatory gene transcription (NF-kB inhibition); des-CIC reversibly conjugates with intracellular fatty acids, forming a lipophilic depot that slowly releases active drug.

display_name: Mometasone Furoate Inhalation Powder / Nasal Spray
description: A potent synthetic 17-heterocyclic corticosteroid with negligible systemic bioavailability (<1%), widely used as a once-daily inhaled therapy for asthma and the premier topical spray for allergic rhinitis and nasal polyps.
strengths: 100 mcg; 200 mcg per actuation (Twisthaler / pMDI); 50 mcg/actuation nasal spray (Nasonex); 0.1% topical cream/ointment (Elocon)
dosage_forms: Dry Powder Inhaler (Twisthaler); Pressurized Metered-Dose Inhaler; Nasal Spray; Topical Cream / Ointment
mechanism_of_action: High-potency glucocorticoid; binds with ultra-high affinity to human glucocorticoid receptors (significantly higher affinity than fluticasone, budesonide, and dexamethasone); suppresses multiple inflammatory genes via NF-kB and AP-1 inhibition; inhibits leukotriene and cytokine release from respiratory mucosal cells.

description: An oral once-daily selective phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor that targets systemic and airway inflammation to reduce exacerbations in severe COPD associated with chronic bronchitis.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and competitively inhibits phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4), the predominant cAMP-metabolizing enzyme in immune and inflammatory cells (neutrophils, macrophages, CD8+ T cells, bronchial smooth muscle); elevates intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP), suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine release.

description: A novel xanthine derivative with phosphodiesterase inhibitory and anti-inflammatory activity that lacks adenosine receptor affinity, providing bronchodilation with dramatically reduced cardiac and CNS toxicities compared to theophylline.
strengths: 400 mg; 100 mg/5 mL syrup; 100 mg/5 mL injection
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Oral Syrup; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits phosphodiesterase (PDE) enzymes, elevating intracellular cAMP in airway smooth muscle; CRITICALLY LACKS AFFINITY FOR ADENOSINE (A1, A2A, A2B) RECEPTORS and does NOT block calcium channels; suppresses inflammatory cell migration and reduces airway hyperreactivity.

description: A secretolytic and secretomotor mucolytic agent that stimulates pulmonary surfactant production, clears viscous bronchial mucus, and possesses local anesthetic and anti-inflammatory properties.
strengths: 30 mg; 75 mg SR; 15 mg/5 mL, 30 mg/5 mL syrup; 15 mg/2 mL ampoule
dosage_forms: Tablet; Sustained-Release Capsule; Oral Syrup; Solution for Injection / Inhalation
mechanism_of_action: Cleaves acidic mucopolysaccharide fibers in bronchial mucus, fragmenting high-molecular-weight polymers; directly stimulates Clara cells and alveolar type II pneumocytes to synthesize and secrete pulmonary surfactant; enhances ciliary beat frequency (mucociliary clearance); blocks neuronal voltage-gated sodium channels, providing throat-soothing local anesthesia.

description: A classic benzylamine secretolytic mucolytic derived from the Indian plant Adhatoda vasica (Vasaka), metabolized in vivo to active ambroxol to liquefy tenaciously thick phlegm.
mechanism_of_action: Derived from the alkaloid vasicine; hydrolyzed in vivo to its primary active metabolite ambroxol; depolymerizes mucopolysaccharide protein fibers and stimulates lysosomal enzyme release from mucus-secreting goblet cells; increases serous bronchial gland secretion.

description: A mucoregulatory agent that alters glycoprotein synthesis to restore the physiological balance of sialomucins and fucomucins, proven in the landmark PEACE study to reduce COPD exacerbations.
strengths: 375 mg; 750 mg; 250 mg/5 mL, 750 mg/5 mL syrup
mechanism_of_action: Acts intracellularly on bronchial goblet cells as a mucoregulator: stimulates sialyltransferase to increase the synthesis of fluid sialomucins while suppressing the production of thick, viscous fucomucins; restores normal viscoelastic properties of bronchial secretions without breaking disulfide bonds.

description: A modern, highly selective, non-sedating second-generation H1-antihistamine with zero hepatic CYP metabolism and zero brain H1-receptor occupancy, used for allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
strengths: 20 mg; 10 mg orally disintegrating tablet (ODT); 2.5 mg/mL oral solution
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Orally Disintegrating Tablet; Oral Solution
mechanism_of_action: Potent, highly selective, and non-competitive peripheral histamine H1-receptor antagonist; completely lacks affinity for muscarinic, adrenergic, serotonergic, or other histamine receptor subtypes; substrate for P-glycoprotein efflux at the blood-brain barrier, resulting in near-zero brain H1-receptor occupancy.

description: A dual-action second-generation antihistamine and platelet-activating factor (PAF) receptor antagonist, providing superior relief of severe nasal congestion and allergic inflammation.
mechanism_of_action: Dual molecular mechanism: selectively blocks peripheral histamine H1 receptors AND antagonizes platelet-activating factor (PAF) receptors; PAF is a potent non-histamine mediator of mucosal edema, severe nasal congestion, bronchial hyperreactivity, and vascular hyperpermeability.

description: A long-acting second-generation H1-receptor antagonist prodrug rapidly converted by CYP3A4 to active carebastine, providing 24-hour non-sedating relief of allergic rhinitis and chronic urticaria.
strengths: 10 mg; 20 mg; 10 mg, 20 mg orally disintegrating tablets (Fast-Tab)
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug rapidly and almost completely converted in the liver by CYP3A4 to active carebastine; carebastine is a potent, long-acting, selective peripheral H1-receptor antagonist with negligible penetration into the central nervous system.

description: A dual-action second-generation H1-receptor antagonist and 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX) inhibitor, combining antihistaminic and anti-leukotriene actions for allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and competitively blocks peripheral histamine H1 receptors; concurrently inhibits 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX), suppressing the biosynthesis of inflammatory leukotrienes (LTB4, LTC4); also inhibits mast cell degranulation and ICAM-1 expression.

description: A dual-action mast cell stabilizer and selective H1-antihistamine, serving as the gold standard topical agent for allergic conjunctivitis and allergic rhinitis.
strengths: 0.1% eye drops (Patanol - BID); 0.2% eye drops (Pataday - once daily); 0.7% eye drops (Pazeo - once daily); 0.6% nasal spray (Patanase)
mechanism_of_action: Dual pharmacological action: selectively and competitively antagonizes histamine H1 receptors, AND stabilizes mast cell membranes, preventing antigen-induced degranulation and release of histamine, leukotrienes, and pro-inflammatory cytokines; inhibits human conjunctival epithelial cell cytokine release.

description: A fast-acting, second-generation topical H1-antihistamine and mast cell stabilizer that relieves nasal symptoms within 15 minutes, co-formulated with fluticasone propionate (Dymista) for severe allergic rhinitis.
strengths: 0.1% nasal spray (137 mcg/spray); 0.15% nasal spray (205.5 mcg/spray); 0.05% eye drops
mechanism_of_action: Multiple anti-allergic actions: potent, competitive antagonist at peripheral histamine H1 receptors; stabilizes mast cell membranes, inhibiting antigen-triggered histamine release; down-regulates ICAM-1 expression and inhibits pro-inflammatory leukotriene and endothelin-1 generation.

description: A semi-synthetic penicillinase-resistant isoxazolyl penicillin active against penicillinase-producing staphylococci, used for MSSA skin, soft tissue, and respiratory tract infections.
strengths: 250 mg; 500 mg; 250 mg vial; 500 mg vial
dosage_forms: Capsule; Powder for Injection; Oral Solution
mechanism_of_action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting the transpeptidation step of peptidoglycan synthesis; bulky isoxazolyl side chain prevents degradation by staphylococcal beta-lactamase.

description: A parenteral penicillinase-resistant isoxazolyl penicillin indicated for severe systemic methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) infections including bacteremia, endocarditis, and osteomyelitis.
strengths: 500 mg vial; 1 g vial; 2 g vial
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), causing cell wall weakening and osmotic lysis; stable against staphylococcal beta-lactamases.

description: An ultra-long-acting repository intramuscular penicillin that releases penicillin G over 3 to 4 weeks, serving as the global first-line curative therapy for syphilis and secondary prophylaxis of rheumatic fever.
strengths: 600,000 units vial; 1,200,000 units (1.2 MU) vial; 2,400,000 units (2.4 MU) vial
dosage_forms: Sterile Suspension for Deep IM Injection
mechanism_of_action: Slowly releases penicillin G from the deep intramuscular depot; penicillin G binds to bacterial PBPs, inhibiting cross-linking of peptidoglycan chains, resulting in bacterial lysis.

description: A natural parenteral penicillin with high intrinsic potency against sensitive streptococci, Neisseria meningitidis, Treponema pallidum (neurosyphilis), and clostridial infections.
strengths: 1,000,000 units (1 MU) vial; 5,000,000 units (5 MU) vial
mechanism_of_action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting transpeptidase enzymes that cross-link peptidoglycan polymers in bacterial cell walls, triggering autolysins and osmotic cell death.

description: A second-generation cephamycin antibiotic with potent anaerobic activity against Bacteroides fragilis, used for surgical prophylaxis and mixed pelvic and intra-abdominal infections.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis; 7-alpha-methoxy group on the beta-lactam ring confers extreme stability against beta-lactamases produced by anaerobic bacteria.

description: A classical parenteral cephamycin with high beta-lactamase resistance and anaerobic efficacy against Bacteroides fragilis, used for surgical prophylaxis and pelvic inflammatory disease.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), causing bacterial cell wall synthesis inhibition; 7-alpha-methoxy group provides extreme resistance to inactivation by Gram-negative and anaerobic beta-lactamases.

description: A propionic acid derivative NSAID with analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic actions, inhibiting COX enzymes and leukocyte migration.
mechanism_of_action: Reversible inhibition of cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), thereby reducing prostaglandin synthesis; also exerts mild inhibition of lipoxygenase.

description: An oxicam-class NSAID with potent analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties, characterised by a relatively short elimination half-life.
dosage_forms: Tablet; Rapid-release Tablet; Powder for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Potent balanced inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-1 and cyclooxygenase-2, suppressing prostaglandin biosynthesis and IL-6 release.

description: The pharmacologically active (S)-(+)-enantiomer of ketoprofen formulated with trometamol for rapid absorption and analgesia at half the racemic dose.
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Solution for Injection; Gel
mechanism_of_action: Selective activation of analgesia by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis through COX-1 and COX-2 blockade, with higher chiral potency than the racemic mixture.

description: A non-acidic prodrug NSAID that is metabolized in the liver to 6-methoxy-2-naphthylacetic acid (6-MNA), with reduced direct gastric mucosal toxicity.
mechanism_of_action: Inactive prodrug converted in the liver to 6-MNA, which preferentially inhibits COX-2 over COX-1, reducing inflammatory prostaglandins.

description: An indene derivative prodrug NSAID whose sulfide metabolite reversibly inhibits COX enzymes; historically noted for relative renal-sparing characteristics.
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug reduced in vivo to active sulindac sulfide, which inhibits COX-1 and COX-2; active metabolite undergoes enterohepatic circulation and renal oxidation back to inactive sulfoxide.

description: A semi-synthetic 14-membered ring macrolide antibiotic with high oral bioavailability and long half-life, used for respiratory, skin, and genital tract infections.
mechanism_of_action: Binds reversibly to the 50S subunit of bacterial 70S ribosomes, inhibiting translocation and peptide chain elongation, blocking bacterial protein synthesis.

description: A fourth-generation 'respiratory' fluoroquinolone with enhanced Gram-positive, anaerobic, and atypical coverage, widely used for pneumonia, tuberculosis, and intra-abdominal infections.
strengths: 400 mg; 400 mg/250 mL IV infusion; 0.5% eye drops
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Solution for Infusion; Ophthalmic Solution
mechanism_of_action: Bactericidal dual-target inhibition of bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, preventing DNA replication, transcription, and repair.

description: A second-generation broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone widely utilized in India for gastrointestinal infections, enteric fever, and genitourinary tract infections.
strengths: 100 mg DT; 200 mg; 400 mg; 200 mg/100 mL IV infusion; 0.3% eye/ear drops
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Dispersible Tablet; IV Infusion; Ophthalmic/Otic Drops
mechanism_of_action: Bactericidal inhibition of DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, halting bacterial chromosome supercoiling, transcription, and division.

description: A synthetic fluoroquinolone that achieves very high concentrations in the urinary tract and gastrointestinal lumen with low systemic tissue levels, making it ideal for UTIs and bacterial diarrhoea.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, preventing DNA supercoiling, synthesis, and cell division.

description: An orally bioavailable penem antibiotic with high stability against extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs), used for resistant respiratory, ENT, and urinary tract infections.
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Dispersible Tablet; Dry Syrup
mechanism_of_action: Binds with high affinity to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), primarily PBP1A, 1B, 2, and 3, inhibiting peptidoglycan cell wall cross-linking and triggering autolysis.

description: A semi-synthetic ketolide antibiotic derived from erythromycin, engineered to overcome macrolide resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to two distinct domains (II and V) on the 23S rRNA of the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit, maintaining high affinity even against MLSB-resistant strains.

description: An advanced fluoroquinolone with potent dual-targeting against bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, specifically indicated for acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis and mild-to-moderate CAP.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits both topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, resulting in rapid bacterial DNA fragmentation and cell death.

description: A glycopeptide antibiotic related to vancomycin with lower nephrotoxicity and red-man syndrome rates, administered once daily or via intramuscular injection for serious Gram-positive infections.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis by binding tightly to the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of cell wall precursor pentapeptides, preventing polymerization.

description: A parenteral third-generation cephalosporin with excellent cerebrospinal fluid penetration, widely used for neonatal sepsis, bacterial meningitis, and serious systemic infections.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting bacterial peptidoglycan cell wall synthesis, resulting in cell wall lysis and bacterial death.

description: A fourth-generation parenteral cephalosporin with zwitterionic structure providing rapid penetration across outer bacterial membranes, highly active against Pseudomonas and Enterobacteriaceae.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to multiple penicillin-binding proteins (PBP2, PBP3, PBP1a/1b) inhibiting peptidoglycan synthesis; zwitterionic charge allows rapid diffusion through outer membrane porins.

description: A third-generation parenteral cephalosporin with potent antipseudomonal activity, used for hospital-acquired infections, febrile neutropenia, and melioidosis.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to essential penicillin-binding proteins (PBP3), inhibiting peptidoglycan synthesis and producing filamentation and lysis of bacterial cells.

description: A first-generation parenteral cephalosporin with excellent activity against MSSA and Streptococcus, established worldwide as the gold standard for surgical antibiotic prophylaxis.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to bacterial penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting cross-linking of peptidoglycan in the cell wall, causing cell lysis.

description: An oral first-generation cephalosporin with prolonged urinary and tissue persistence, used once or twice daily for skin, pharyngeal, and urinary tract infections.
strengths: 125 mg DT; 250 mg DT; 500 mg; 1 g
dosage_forms: Dispersible Tablet; Film-coated Tablet; Oral Suspension
mechanism_of_action: Bactericidal inhibition of cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), halting peptidoglycan assembly.

description: A second-generation oral cephalosporin with enhanced activity against Haemophilus influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis, used for upper and lower respiratory infections.
strengths: 125 mg DT; 250 mg; 375 mg ER; 500 mg
dosage_forms: Capsule; Dispersible Tablet; Extended-Release Tablet; Oral Suspension
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), leading to bacterial lysis.

description: An oral third-generation cephalosporin prodrug with enhanced affinity for penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae and common respiratory pathogens.
mechanism_of_action: Hydrolyzed by esterases during absorption to active cefditoren, which binds to PBPs and inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis.

description: An injectable aminopenicillin combined with a beta-lactamase inhibitor, providing broad coverage against beta-lactamase producing organisms, anaerobes, and Acinetobacter baumannii.
mechanism_of_action: Ampicillin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis; sulbactam irreversibly binds and inactivates beta-lactamases and has intrinsic bactericidal activity against Acinetobacter baumannii PBPs.

description: An advanced antipseudomonal cephalosporin combined with a beta-lactamase inhibitor, engineered specifically to overcome multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
strengths: 1.5 g vial (1 g ceftolozane / 0.5 g tazobactam); 3 g vial (2 g ceftolozane / 1 g tazobactam)
dosage_forms: Powder for Concentrate for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Ceftolozane inhibits PBPs (PBP1b, PBP1c, PBP3) with high affinity and resistance to ampC hydrolysis and efflux pumps; tazobactam protects against most class A and class C beta-lactamases.

description: A novel beta-lactam / non-beta-lactam diazabicyclooctane beta-lactamase inhibitor combination active against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (KPC, OXA-48).
strengths: 2.5 g vial (2 g ceftazidime / 0.5 g avibactam)
dosage_forms: Powder for Concentrate for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Ceftazidime inhibits cell wall synthesis; avibactam is a non-beta-lactam beta-lactamase inhibitor that reversibly inhibits Class A (KPC), Class C (AmpC), and some Class D (OXA-48) beta-lactamases via covalent carbamylation.

description: A polymyxin antibiotic prodrug acting as a cationic detergent against Gram-negative outer membranes, reserved for extensively drug-resistant (XDR) pathogens.
strengths: 1 million IU (approx. 80 mg CMS); 2 million IU; 3 million IU vial; 4.5 million IU vial
dosage_forms: Powder for Solution for Injection/Infusion or Inhalation
mechanism_of_action: Binds to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and phospholipids in the outer cell membrane of Gram-negative bacteria, displacing calcium and magnesium, causing membrane disruption and leakage of intracellular contents.

description: An active polymyxin antibiotic administered directly as active drug (not a prodrug), preferred over colistin for systemic bloodstream infections due to predictable pharmacokinetics and lower renal dependency.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to anionic lipid A portion of LPS in bacterial outer membrane, destabilizing membrane integrity and causing osmotic leakage of cellular contents.

description: A first-in-class glycylcycline antibiotic overcoming classical tetracycline efflux and ribosomal protection mechanisms, used for complicated skin, soft tissue, and intra-abdominal infections.
mechanism_of_action: Binds reversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit with 5 times higher affinity than minocycline, halting peptide chain growth and overcoming classical tetracycline efflux pumps and ribosomal protection proteins.

description: A highly lipophilic second-generation tetracycline with excellent tissue and CNS penetration, widely used for moderate-to-severe acne vulgaris, MRSA skin infections, and multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter.
dosage_forms: Capsule; Tablet; Extended-Release Tablet; Powder for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit, preventing entry of aminoacyl-tRNA into the ribosomal acceptor (A) site, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis; also possesses anti-inflammatory and matrix metalloproteinase inhibitory properties.

description: A potent aminoglycoside antibiotic with superior intrinsic activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa compared to gentamicin, administered IV or via inhalation for cystic fibrosis.
strengths: 20 mg/2 mL; 80 mg/2 mL vial; 300 mg/5 mL inhalation solution; 0.3% eye drops
dosage_forms: Solution for Injection; Inhalation Solution; Ophthalmic Drops
mechanism_of_action: Binds irreversibly to the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of genetic code and premature termination of peptide chain synthesis, leading to cell membrane damage and bactericidal death.

description: A semi-synthetic aminoglycoside antibiotic derived from sisomicin with resistance to several bacterial modifying enzymes and demonstrably lower ototoxicity than gentamicin.
strengths: 25 mg/mL; 100 mg/mL; 300 mg/3 mL vial; 0.3% eye drops
mechanism_of_action: Binds irreversibly to the 30S bacterial ribosomal subunit, interfering with initiation complex formation and causing misreading of mRNA, leading to rapid bactericidal killing.

description: An aminoglycoside antibiotic with bactericidal activity against aerobic Gram-negative bacilli and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, reserved for MDR-TB and serious hospital infections.
dosage_forms: Powder for Injection; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Binds irreversibly to the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of codons and inhibition of translocation, terminating bacterial protein synthesis.

description: A broad-spectrum classical antibiotic with excellent CSF penetration, reserved for life-threatening infections such as bacterial meningitis and rickettsial diseases when other options fail.
strengths: 250 mg; 500 mg; 1 g vial; 0.5% eye drops; 1% eye ointment
dosage_forms: Capsule; Powder for Injection; Ophthalmic Solution; Ophthalmic Ointment
mechanism_of_action: Binds reversibly to the 50S subunit of 70S bacterial ribosomes, inhibiting the peptidyl transferase reaction and preventing peptide bond formation.

active_ingredient: Pristinamycin (mixture of pristinamycin IA and IIA)
description: An oral streptogramin antibiotic consisting of a synergistic combination of two factors (IA and IIA), used for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and refractory streptococcal infections.
mechanism_of_action: Consists of pristinamycin IA (a macrolactone) and IIA (a polyunsaturated macrolactone) that bind sequentially to separate sites on the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit; binding of IIA increases affinity for IA by 100-fold, transforming bacteriostatic action into bactericidal inhibition.

description: A second-generation oxazolidinone antibiotic 4 to 8 times more potent than linezolid, administered once daily for 6 days for acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI).
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Lyophilized Powder for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug converted by plasma phosphatases to active tedizolid, which binds to the 23S rRNA of the 50S bacterial ribosomal subunit, inhibiting initiation complex formation and protein synthesis.

description: A second-generation lipoglycopeptide antibiotic with an ultra-long terminal half-life of 14 days, permitting complete therapy of acute bacterial skin infections in one or two doses.
dosage_forms: Lyophilized Powder for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Binds to the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of growing bacterial peptidoglycan chains, blocking transglycosylation and transpeptidation; lipophilic side chain anchors to membrane, increasing potency.

description: A cyclic lipopeptide bactericidal antibiotic that binds to and depolarizes bacterial cell membranes, used for MRSA bacteremia, right-sided infective endocarditis, and severe skin infections.
mechanism_of_action: Binds in a calcium-dependent manner to bacterial cell membranes, oligomerizes, and inserts into the lipid bilayer, creating pores that cause rapid potassium ion efflux, membrane depolarization, and cessation of DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis without cell lysis.

description: A second-generation broad-spectrum triazole antifungal agent, established as the first-line treatment of choice for invasive aspergillosis.
dosage_forms: Film-coated Tablet; Powder for Solution for Infusion; Oral Suspension
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent 14-alpha-sterol demethylase, blocking the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol, leading to accumulation of toxic 14-methylated sterols and fungal cell membrane lysis.

description: An extended-spectrum triazole antifungal with potent activity against Aspergillus, Candida, and Mucorales (zygomycetes), widely used for prophylaxis in hematological malignancy and salvage therapy.
strengths: 100 mg delayed-release tablet; 300 mg/16.7 mL IV vial; 40 mg/mL oral suspension
dosage_forms: Delayed-Release Tablet; Solution for Infusion; Oral Suspension
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, disrupting ergosterol synthesis and destabilizing the fungal cell membrane.

description: A first-in-class parenteral echinocandin antifungal that inhibits fungal cell wall synthesis, used for invasive candidiasis, esophageal candidiasis, and salvage therapy for invasive aspergillosis.
dosage_forms: Lyophilized Powder for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Non-competitively inhibits beta-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase, an enzyme absent in mammalian cells, preventing synthesis of beta-(1,3)-D-glucan in the fungal cell wall, causing osmotic fragility and lysis.

description: A second-generation echinocandin antifungal with no loading dose requirement, used for invasive candidiasis, candidemia, and antifungal prophylaxis in stem cell transplantation.
dosage_forms: Lyophilized Powder for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Non-competitively inhibits 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase, disrupting fungal cell wall integrity and leading to osmotic lysis.

description: A potent topical imidazole antifungal with exceptionally low minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) against dermatophytes, permitting once-daily application for only 1 to 2 weeks.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, disrupting ergosterol synthesis in fungal cell membranes; uniquely incorporates an optically active R-enantiomer dithioacetal structure providing extreme affinity for dermatophyte enzymes.

description: A long-acting propionic acid NSAID suitable for once-daily dosing in chronic inflammatory joint disorders.
mechanism_of_action: Non-selective inhibition of cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), halting the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins.

description: A propionic acid derivative NSAID available in systemic, ophthalmic and throat lozenge formulations for targeted anti-inflammatory and analgesic therapy.
strengths: 50 mg; 100 mg; 8.75 mg lozenges; 0.03% eye drops
mechanism_of_action: Reversibly inhibits cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2), suppressing prostaglandin synthesis in both systemic and ocular tissues.

description: An anthranilic acid derivative (fenamate) NSAID used extensively for the acute abortive treatment of migraine attacks and inflammatory joint disorders.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes to reduce prostaglandin synthesis, and uniquely exerts direct antagonist actions at prostaglandin receptor sites.

description: A pyranocarboxylic acid NSAID exhibiting preferential inhibition of COX-2 over COX-1, providing anti-inflammatory efficacy with a relatively favourable gastric profile.
mechanism_of_action: Preferentially inhibits cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) over COX-1, diminishing inflammatory prostaglandins at sites of joint inflammation while partially sparing mucosal COX-1.

description: An injectable water-soluble prodrug of valdecoxib, providing selective COX-2 inhibition for short-term post-operative acute pain control without affecting platelet aggregation.
mechanism_of_action: Rapidly converted by enzymatic hydrolysis in the liver to valdecoxib, a highly selective inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2).

description: An alkaloid derived from Colchicum autumnale that disrupts microtubule polymerization, selectively inhibiting neutrophil chemotaxis in acute gout and Mediterranean fever.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to tubulin dimers, preventing microtubule assembly; suppresses neutrophil extravasation, degranulation, and inflammasome activation (NLRP3) triggered by monosodium urate crystals.

description: A potent non-purine selective inhibitor of xanthine oxidase, providing significant serum uric acid reduction for chronic gout without hypersensitivity cross-reactivity to allopurinol.
mechanism_of_action: Potently and selectively inhibits both the oxidized and reduced forms of xanthine oxidase by blocking the pterin-binding channel, decreasing uric acid production.

description: A semi-synthetic sulfur derivative of colchicoside with selective GABAA and glycinergic receptor agonist properties, widely prescribed in India for acute painful muscle spasm.
strengths: 4 mg; 8 mg; 4 mg/2 mL injection; 0.25% ointment
dosage_forms: Capsule; Tablet; Solution for Injection; Ointment
mechanism_of_action: Selective agonist at GABA-A and strychnine-sensitive glycine receptors in the spinal cord and brainstem; decreases motor neuron excitability without curare-like muscle paralysis.

description: A centrally acting GABA-B receptor agonist that suppresses monosynaptic and polysynaptic spinal reflexes, relieving spasticity resulting from multiple sclerosis and spinal cord lesions.
mechanism_of_action: Specific agonist at presynaptic and postsynaptic GABA-B receptors in the spinal cord; inhibits calcium influx, reducing the release of excitatory neurotransmitters (glutamate, aspartate).

description: A centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonist that reduces muscle spasticity by promoting presynaptic inhibition of motor neurons, with minimal muscle weakness.
mechanism_of_action: Selective agonist at central presynaptic alpha-2 adrenergic receptors; decreases the release of excitatory amino acids from spinal interneurons.

description: A centrally acting muscle relaxant used as an adjunct in acute painful musculoskeletal conditions, acting primarily at spinal and subcortical levels.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits multisynaptic reflex arcs involved in producing and maintaining skeletal muscle spasm at spinal cord and subcortical areas.

description: A centrally acting muscle relaxant with membrane-stabilizing and sodium-channel blocking actions that reduces muscle spasticity and tone without significant sedation.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits voltage-gated sodium channels, stabilizing neuronal membranes; depresses mono- and polysynaptic spinal cord reflex pathways and reticulospinal tract transmission.

description: A tricyclic-structured central muscle relaxant that reduces tonic somatic motor activity primarily within the brainstem, relieving acute muscle spasm.
strengths: 5 mg; 10 mg; 15 mg ER; 30 mg ER
mechanism_of_action: Acts primarily within the brainstem at the locus coeruleus; enhances norepinephrine-mediated inhibition of gamma and alpha motor systems, reducing muscle spasm.

description: A non-opioid, non-NSAID centrally acting analgesic that inhibits monoamine reuptake and modulates voltage-sensitive calcium/sodium channels, devoid of respiratory depression.
mechanism_of_action: Triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor (serotonin, norepinephrine, dopamine) and inhibitor of voltage-gated calcium/sodium channels in central nociceptive pathways.

description: A high-affinity partial agonist at mu-opioid receptors and antagonist at kappa receptors, with a ceiling effect on respiratory depression, used for chronic pain and opioid dependence.
strengths: 0.2 mg sublingual; 2 mg; 8 mg; 5 mcg/hr patch; 10 mcg/hr patch; 20 mcg/hr patch; 0.3 mg/mL injection
dosage_forms: Sublingual Tablet; Transdermal Patch; Solution for Injection
mechanism_of_action: Partial agonist at mu-opioid receptors with very high affinity and slow receptor dissociation rate; antagonist at kappa-opioid and ORL-1 receptors.

description: A potent synthetic mu-opioid receptor agonist (50-100 times more potent than morphine) utilized for anaesthesia, breakthrough cancer pain, and transdermal chronic pain management.
strengths: 12 mcg/hr patch; 25 mcg/hr patch; 50 mcg/hr patch; 100 mcg/hr patch; 50 mcg/mL injection; 100 mcg lozenge
dosage_forms: Transdermal Patch; Solution for Injection; Buccal Lozenge / Film
mechanism_of_action: Selective and potent agonist at mu-opioid receptors in the central nervous system; inhibits adenylate cyclase, hyperpolarizes neurons, and reduces nociceptive transmission.

description: A semi-synthetic pure mu-opioid receptor agonist with high oral bioavailability, used in immediate- and controlled-release formulations for severe pain.
strengths: 5 mg; 10 mg; 20 mg; 40 mg; 80 mg CR
dosage_forms: Immediate-Release Tablet; Controlled-Release Tablet; Oral Solution
mechanism_of_action: Full agonist at mu-opioid receptors with some affinity for kappa- and delta-opioid receptors; inhibits adenylyl cyclase, opening potassium channels and blocking presynaptic calcium influx.

description: A long-acting synthetic mu-opioid agonist and NMDA receptor antagonist used for opioid dependence maintenance and refractory neuropathic cancer pain.
strengths: 5 mg; 10 mg; 40 mg dispersible; 5 mg/5 mL oral solution; 10 mg/mL injection
dosage_forms: Tablet; Dispersible Tablet; Oral Solution; Injection
mechanism_of_action: Agonist at mu-opioid receptors, antagonist at NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptors, and inhibitor of serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake.

description: A benzomorphan opioid with kappa-opioid agonist and weak mu-antagonist/partial agonist properties, frequently formulated with naloxone to prevent intravenous abuse.
mechanism_of_action: Agonist at kappa-opioid receptors producing spinal analgesia and sedation; weak antagonist or partial agonist at mu-opioid receptors; binds sigma receptors.

description: A semi-synthetic phenanthrene opioid mu-agonist with antitussive and analgesic actions, widely prescribed in combination with paracetamol for moderate to severe pain.
mechanism_of_action: Pure agonist at mu-opioid receptors; inhibits ascending pain pathways and suppresses the medullary cough reflex center.

description: A third-generation highly cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic blocker with nitric oxide-mediated endothelial vasodilation and neutral metabolic profile.
