mechanism_of_action: Dual mechanism: highly selective competitive beta-1 adrenergic antagonist, and stimulates endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) via beta-3 adrenergic receptors, releasing nitric oxide and causing peripheral vasodilation.

description: A non-selective competitive beta-blocker with postsynaptic alpha-1 adrenergic blocking activity, established as the first-line drug of choice for hypertensive emergencies and hypertension in pregnancy.
strengths: 100 mg; 200 mg; 5 mg/mL (20 mL IV ampoule)
mechanism_of_action: Competitively blocks beta-1, beta-2, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors; oral ratio of alpha:beta blockade is approx. 1:3; IV ratio is approx. 1:7; alpha-1 blockade reduces systemic vascular resistance while beta-1 blockade prevents reflex tachycardia.

description: An ultra-short-acting, cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic blocker metabolized rapidly by red blood cell esterases, used for rapid intraoperative and emergency control of supraventricular tachycardia and aortic dissection.
strengths: 100 mg/10 mL vial; 2.5 g/10 mL ampoule for infusion
dosage_forms: Solution for Injection; Concentrate for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Selective competitive antagonist at myocardial beta-1 adrenergic receptors with negligible intrinsic sympathomimetic or membrane-stabilizing activity; rapidly hydrolyzed by cytoplasmic esterases in red blood cells.

description: A long-acting, lipophilic prodrug ACE inhibitor that provides sustained 24-hour tissue ACE inhibition, extensive endothelial protection, and proven reduction of cardiovascular events in stable coronary artery disease.
strengths: 2 mg; 4 mg; 8 mg (erbumine); 2.5 mg; 5 mg; 10 mg (arginine)
mechanism_of_action: Hydrolyzed in the liver to active metabolite perindoprilat, which competitively inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), blocking conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, decreasing aldosterone, and inhibiting bradykinin degradation.

description: An ester prodrug angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) with insurmountable, tight AT1-receptor binding kinetics, proven to reduce cardiovascular mortality and hospitalizations in heart failure (CHARM trial).
mechanism_of_action: Completely bioactivated during gastrointestinal absorption to active candesartan, which binds selectively and insurmountably to the AT1 receptor with high affinity and slow dissociation, blocking vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion.

description: A unique fourth-generation dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with dual L-type and N-type calcium channel blockade, suppressing sympathetic nerve activity and significantly reducing pedal oedema and proteinuria.
mechanism_of_action: Dual blockade: blocks L-type voltage-gated calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle cells (causing arterial vasodilation) AND N-type calcium channels at sympathetic nerve endings (inhibiting norepinephrine release and sympathetic overactivity).

description: A triple L-, T-, and N-type calcium channel blocker with high vascular membrane affinity, conferring long-lasting 24-hour antihypertensive, cardioprotective, and renoprotective effects with minimal pedal oedema.
mechanism_of_action: Triple calcium channel blocker: blocks L-type channels (arteriolar dilation), T-type channels (aldosterone suppression and cardiac protective effect), and N-type channels (sympathetic nerve inhibition and efferent arteriolar dilation).

description: A selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) with high specificity for aldosterone receptors, proven to reduce mortality in heart failure post-MI without the antiandrogenic side effects of spironolactone.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively binds to the mineralocorticoid receptor, competitively blocking aldosterone binding in the renal distal tubule and collecting duct; prevents sodium and water reabsorption while conserving potassium and magnesium; attenuates myocardial and vascular fibrosis.

description: A non-thiazide chlorosulfamoyl indole diuretic with dual diuretic and direct vascular smooth muscle vasodilating properties, established in major trials (HYVET, ADVANCE) for stroke and mortality reduction.
mechanism_of_action: Dual action: inhibits sodium and chloride reabsorption in the early distal convoluted tubule (producing saluresis), AND directly reduces vascular reactivity to pressor amines by modulating transmembrane calcium influx in arterial smooth muscle cells.

description: A selective and specific hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) pacemaker channel inhibitor that lowers heart rate without reducing myocardial contractility or blood pressure.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks the hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel (If 'funny' pacemaker current) in the sinoatrial node, slowing the diastolic depolarization slope and reducing heart rate at rest and during exercise.

description: A novel water-soluble triazole prodrug with broad-spectrum activity against invasive aspergillosis and mucormycosis, notable for causing QTc shortening rather than prolongation.
dosage_forms: Capsule; Powder for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Rapidly hydrolyzed by plasma esterases to active isavuconazole, which inhibits fungal 14-alpha-lanosterol demethylase, blocking ergosterol synthesis.

description: A semi-synthetic echinocandin antifungal that undergoes non-enzymatic chemical degradation, making it completely independent of renal and hepatic metabolism.
mechanism_of_action: Non-competitively inhibits 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase, halting fungal cell wall synthesis and causing osmotic lysis.

description: A topical broad-spectrum imidazole antifungal containing a unique benzothiophene ring, providing dual fungistatic and direct fungicidal action with potent anti-inflammatory and antipruritic properties.
strengths: 2% cream; 2% lotion; 2% dust powder; 500 mg vaginal suppository
dosage_forms: Topical Cream; Topical Lotion; Topical Powder; Vaginal Tablet
mechanism_of_action: Dual mechanism: at low concentrations, inhibits 14-alpha-demethylase blocking ergosterol synthesis; at higher concentrations, benzothiophene ring directly inserts into fungal plasma membrane, forming pores and causing immediate cell death.

description: A morpholine antifungal nail lacquer and cream with a unique dual-enzyme inhibition mechanism in the ergosterol pathway, applied once or twice weekly for onychomycosis.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits two separate fungal enzymes in the ergosterol biosynthesis pathway: delta-14-reductase and delta-7,delta-8-isomerase, depleting ergosterol and causing accumulation of toxic ignosterol.

description: An oral fungistatic antifungal that binds to fungal tubulin and concentrates in newly formed keratin, established as the gold standard for tinea capitis (scalp ringworm) in children.
strengths: 125 mg; 250 mg; 500 mg; 125 mg/5 mL suspension
mechanism_of_action: Binds to fungal tubulin and disrupts the mitotic spindle apparatus, arresting fungal cells in metaphase; also binds to human keratin, rendering newly formed hair, skin, and nails resistant to fungal invasion.

description: A fluorinated pyrimidine antifungal that converts intracellularly to 5-fluorouracil, combined synergistically with amphotericin B for cryptococcal meningitis.
strengths: 250 mg; 500 mg; 2.5 g/250 mL IV infusion
mechanism_of_action: Transported into fungal cells by cytosine permease and deaminated by fungal cytosine deaminase to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU); 5-FU inhibits thymidylate synthase and incorporates into fungal RNA, terminating protein and DNA synthesis.

description: A broad-spectrum monophosphoramidate adenosine nucleotide prodrug that halts viral RNA synthesis, used intravenously for COVID-19 in hospitalized and high-risk patients.
dosage_forms: Lyophilized Powder for Injection; Concentrate for Solution for Infusion
mechanism_of_action: Metabolized intracellularly into active remdesivir triphosphate (GS-443902), which competes with ATP for incorporation by viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), causing delayed chain termination at position i+3.

description: An oral ribonucleoside prodrug that induces viral error catastrophe through lethal mutagenesis in viral RNA, used for mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in high-risk outpatients.
mechanism_of_action: Hydrolyzed in blood to N4-hydroxycytidine (NHC), phosphorylated intracellularly to NHC triphosphate, which is utilized by viral RdRp; mispairs with adenine and guanine, inducing massive catastrophic mutations during replication ('error catastrophe').

description: A peptidomimetic inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro / 3CLpro) boosted with ritonavir, reducing COVID-19 hospitalization and death by up to 89% in high-risk patients.
strengths: 300 mg nirmatrelvir (two 150 mg tablets) + 100 mg ritonavir (one 100 mg tablet) per dose
mechanism_of_action: Nirmatrelvir reversible inhibits the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro/3CLpro), preventing processing of viral polyprotein precursors; low-dose ritonavir acts as a pharmacokinetic booster by inhibiting CYP3A4, sustaining therapeutic nirmatrelvir blood levels.

description: A breakthrough nucleotide analogue NS5B polymerase inhibitor with a high genetic barrier to resistance, serving as the backbone of direct-acting antiviral cures for chronic Hepatitis C.
mechanism_of_action: Uridine nucleotide prodrug metabolized in hepatocytes to active 2'-deoxy-2'-alpha-fluoro-beta-C-methyluridine triphosphate (GS-461203); acts as an obligate chain terminator for HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.

description: Third-generation antiepileptic drug selectively enhancing slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels.
strengths: 50 mg; 100 mg; 150 mg; 200 mg; 10 mg/mL syrup; 200 mg/20 mL IV
mechanism_of_action: Selectively enhances slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels, terminating sustained repetitive neuronal firing without affecting fast inactivation.

description: Broad-spectrum phenyltriazine antiepileptic and mood stabilizer targeting voltage-gated sodium and calcium channels.
mechanism_of_action: Voltage-gated sodium channel blocker and inhibitor of presynaptic glutamate and aspartate release.

description: Keto-analog of carbamazepine acting as a prodrug for 10-monohydroxy metabolite (MHD) with lower hepatic enzyme induction.
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug rapidly converted to active 10-monohydroxy metabolite (MHD), which blocks voltage-sensitive sodium channels.

description: Broad-spectrum sulfamate-substituted monosaccharide antiepileptic and migraine prophylactic agent with multiple mechanisms.
mechanism_of_action: Blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels, potentiates GABA-A receptor currents, inhibits AMPA/kainate glutamate receptors, and weakly inhibits carbonic anhydrase (isozymes II and IV).

description: Potent alpha-2-delta ligand that binds presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels to treat neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and anxiety.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively binds the alpha-2-delta auxiliary subunit of presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels in the CNS, reducing calcium influx and subsequent release of glutamate, substance P, and norepinephrine.

description: Gold standard dopamine replacement therapy for Parkinson disease combining dopamine precursor with peripheral DDC inhibitor.
mechanism_of_action: Levodopa crosses the blood-brain barrier via L-neutral amino acid transporter (LAT1) and is decarboxylated to dopamine in striatal neurons; carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase (DDC), preventing peripheral conversion and nausea.

description: Reversible, non-competitive, piperidine-based acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used to improve cognitive function in Alzheimer disease.
strengths: 5 mg; 10 mg; 10 mg orally disintegrating tablet (ODT)
mechanism_of_action: Reversibly and non-competitively inhibits acetylcholinesterase (AChE), increasing acetylcholine concentration in cortical synapses.

description: Prototypic 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist providing rapid acute relief of migraine attacks and cluster headaches.
strengths: 25 mg; 50 mg; 100 mg; 6 mg/0.5 mL subcutaneous autoinjector; 20 mg nasal spray
mechanism_of_action: Selective agonist for 5-HT1B (vascular) and 5-HT1D (neuronal) receptors, causing cranial vasoconstriction and inhibiting trigeminal calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) release.

description: S-enantiomer of citalopram; the most selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) with minimal anticholinergic and antihistaminic activity.
mechanism_of_action: Pure S-enantiomer that binds with high affinity to the primary serotonin transporter (SERT) and allosteric site, potently blocking 5-HT reuptake.

description: Serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) with dose-dependent dual neurotransmitter modulation.
mechanism_of_action: Potently inhibits serotonin reuptake at low doses (<150 mg/day); additionally inhibits norepinephrine reuptake at moderate-to-high doses (>=150 mg/day).

description: Potent dual SNRI with balanced 5-HT and NE reuptake inhibition across all therapeutic doses, effective for depression and chronic somatic pain.
mechanism_of_action: Potently and equally inhibits neuronal reuptake of both serotonin and norepinephrine throughout the dosing range; weak dopamine uptake inhibitor.

description: Noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant (NaSSA) that stimulates appetite, promotes sleep, and avoids sexual dysfunction.
strengths: 7.5 mg; 15 mg; 30 mg; 45 mg orally disintegrating tablet (ODT)
mechanism_of_action: Antagonizes central presynaptic alpha-2 auto- and heteroreceptors, increasing norepinephrine and serotonin release; simultaneously blocks postsynaptic 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors and potently blocks H1 histamine receptors.

description: Second-generation (atypical) thienobenzodiazepine antipsychotic with broad receptor affinity and high risk of metabolic syndrome.
strengths: 2.5 mg; 5 mg; 7.5 mg; 10 mg; 15 mg; 20 mg orally disintegrating tablet (ODT)
dosage_forms: Tablet; Orally Disintegrating Tablet; IM Injection
mechanism_of_action: Antagonizes dopamine D2, serotonin 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C, histamine H1, muscarinic M1-M5, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors in the CNS.

description: Broad-spectrum dibenzothiazepine atypical antipsychotic with low D2 receptor occupancy, minimal EPS, and potent active metabolite norquetiapine.
strengths: 25 mg; 50 mg; 100 mg; 200 mg; 300 mg; 400 mg extended-release
mechanism_of_action: Low-affinity D2 receptor antagonist with rapid dissociation kinetics ('hit-and-run'); potently antagonizes 5-HT2A, H1 histamine, and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors; active metabolite norquetiapine potently inhibits the norepinephrine transporter (NET) and acts as a 5-HT1A partial agonist.

description: Third-generation atypical antipsychotic acting as a dopamine D2 partial agonist ('dopamine system stabilizer') with favorable metabolic profile.
strengths: 2 mg; 5 mg; 10 mg; 15 mg; 20 mg; 30 mg; 10 mg orally disintegrating tablet (ODT)
mechanism_of_action: Functions as a partial agonist at dopamine D2 and 5-HT1A receptors, and an antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors.

description: Oral retinoid providing curative remission for severe recalcitrant nodulocystic acne; highly teratogenic requiring strict risk management.
mechanism_of_action: Interacts with retinoic acid nuclear receptors, profoundly suppressing sebaceous gland size and activity, normalizing follicular keratinocyte differentiation, reducing Cutibacterium acnes, and exerting potent anti-inflammatory effects.

description: Third-generation synthetic naphthoic acid topical retinoid with high selectivity for RAR-beta and RAR-gamma, offering superior photostability and tolerability.
mechanism_of_action: Binds selectively to nuclear retinoic acid receptor (RAR) beta and gamma subtypes; modulates cellular differentiation, keratinization, and inflammatory processes.

description: Naturally derived pseudomonic acid antibiotic that uniquely inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase, eradicating MRSA and impetigo.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively and reversibly binds to bacterial isoleucyl-transfer RNA (tRNA) synthetase, arresting protein synthesis without cross-resistance to other antibiotic classes.

description: Topical calcineurin inhibitor providing non-steroidal immunosuppression for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis without skin atrophy.
mechanism_of_action: Binds to intracellular immunophilin FKBP-12, creating a complex that inhibits calcineurin phosphatase; blocks dephosphorylation of NFAT, preventing transcription of IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, and TNF-alpha in T-lymphocytes.

description: Super-potent Class I topical corticosteroid for short-term management of severe, recalcitrant inflammatory dermatoses.
mechanism_of_action: High-affinity agonist for glucocorticoid receptors; induces lipocortin synthesis, inhibiting phospholipase A2 and decreasing downstream prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and inflammatory cytokines.

description: Topical allylamine antifungal that inhibits squalene epoxidase, providing fungicidal activity against dermatophytes with short 1-week treatment courses.
mechanism_of_action: Selectively inhibits fungal squalene epoxidase, blocking ergosterol biosynthesis and causing toxic intracellular accumulation of squalene.

description: Narrow-spectrum steroidal antibacterial that inhibits bacterial elongation factor G, highly effective for staphylococcal pyoderma.
mechanism_of_action: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by preventing the translocation of elongation factor G (EF-G) from the bacterial ribosome.

description: Topical ATP-sensitive potassium channel opener and vasodilator that stimulates follicular keratinocytes to treat androgenetic alopecia.
mechanism_of_action: Opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle and hair follicles; upregulates vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), shortens telogen phase, and prolongs anagen (growth) phase of hair follicles.

description: Short-acting bioidentical glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid; the gold-standard intravenous therapy for acute adrenal crisis and septic shock.
strengths: 10 mg; 20 mg tablet; 100 mg / 2 mL IV vial; 1% topical cream
dosage_forms: Tablet; Solution for Injection; Topical Cream
mechanism_of_action: Diffuses across cell membranes and binds to cytosolic glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid receptors, regulating gene transcription to suppress inflammation and maintain vascular tone and electrolyte balance.

description: Intermediate-acting synthetic glucocorticoid with 5 times the anti-inflammatory potency of hydrocortisone and minimal mineralocorticoid activity, used for pulse therapy in acute autoimmune relapses.
strengths: 4 mg; 8 mg; 16 mg; 40 mg IV vial; 125 mg IV vial; 500 mg IV vial; 1000 mg IV vial
mechanism_of_action: Potent glucocorticoid receptor agonist; inhibits inflammatory cytokine synthesis, impairs leukocyte migration, and induces lymphocyte apoptosis.

description: Oxazoline derivative of prednisolone with comparable immunosuppressive efficacy but significantly less bone loss, weight gain, and glucose intolerance.
mechanism_of_action: Prodrug rapidly converted to active 21-desacetyldeflazacort, which binds glucocorticoid receptors to suppress inflammatory cytokines, T-cell activation, and prostaglandin synthesis.

description: Long-acting fluorinated glucocorticoid with zero mineralocorticoid activity, uniquely capable of crossing the placenta to accelerate fetal lung maturation in preterm labor.
strengths: 0.5 mg tablet; 4 mg/mL IV/IM vial; 0.05% topical cream
dosage_forms: Tablet; Solution for Injection; Topical Cream
mechanism_of_action: High-affinity fluorinated glucocorticoid receptor agonist; stimulates synthesis of pulmonary surfactant proteins (SP-A, SP-B) in fetal type II pneumocytes and downregulates pro-inflammatory cascades.

description: Intermediate-acting fluorinated glucocorticoid with zero mineralocorticoid activity, widely formulated as microcrystalline suspension for intra-articular and intralesional therapy.
strengths: 40 mg/mL injectable suspension; 0.1% oral paste; 55 mcg nasal spray
dosage_forms: Injectable Suspension; Oral Paste; Nasal Spray
mechanism_of_action: Potent glucocorticoid receptor agonist; inhibits phospholipase A2 and cyclooxygenase pathways, reducing synovial inflammation, keloid fibroblast proliferation, and allergic rhinitis.
